subject: Order form: output rights & training - clearance needed
messages:
From: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@novaforge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Hart <emma.hart@novaforge.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Dec 2028 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Order form — output rights & training questions

Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft order form yesterday. Our legal team spotted a couple of provisions we need clarified before procurement can sign:

- Section 4.2 (Output ownership): language implies Redwood may use customer outputs for model training unless opted out. We need explicit confirmation that NovaForge outputs will not be used to train public models, and a durable opt-out mechanism.
- Feedback license: the draft grants a broad feedback license — can that be narrowed to non-confidential feedback and for product improvement only?
- Data retention & telemetry: can you provide the evidence checklist your side requires for SOC/environmental compliance?

I've attached a marked-up order form (novaforge_orderform_marked.pdf) to show the specific lines. We're aiming to close this week if possible.

Oliver
Oliver Reed
Head of Procurement, NovaForge
attachments: novaforge_orderform_marked.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@novaforge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Dec 2028 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — output rights & training questions

Oliver — thanks for the marked copy, helpful. Looping in Legal (Laura) and Sales Ops (Ben). Quick answers up front and then a proposed path:

- Short answer on output: Redwood's standard order form allows customer opt-out from training; we also offer an explicit "no-training" amendment for enterprise contracts. I can push a clause that reads: "Customer Data and Customer Output will not be used to train models outside Customer-dedicated instances or for Redwood public model improvements unless Customer provides explicit written consent."

- Feedback license: happy to narrow scope — if we limit it to non-confidential feedback used solely for product improvement and anonymized telemetry, that should be reasonable.

- Evidence checklist: attaching a template (redline_annotations_karthik.docx) and asking Ben to provide the compliance/evidence packet Laura needs to clear procurement.

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura to propose legal language for the two clauses by EOD.
2) Ben to attach evidence checklist + point contact for procurement.
3) If language looks good, schedule 30-min sign-off call with NovaForge legal + procurement.

I can be on the call if helpful.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redline_annotations_karthik.docx (docx, 75KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@novaforge.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Dec 2028 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — output rights & training questions

Karthik/Oliver — I reviewed the marked order form. Suggested edits below (summary), happy to circulate redline if we agree on direction: 

1) Output ownership (Section 4.2): Replace current sentence with: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Outputs. Redwood will not use Customer Outputs to train or improve any models available to third parties, public model weights, or shared model artifacts, except where Customer has provided explicit written consent."

2) Training/data use (Definitions & Opt-out): Add an explicit opt-out checkbox in Exhibit A and a mechanism: "Customer may elect in writing to opt-out of any use of Customer Data or Customer Output for Redwood model training; such election will be applied within thirty (30) days and reflected in the Order Form."

3) Feedback license (new Section): Narrow to: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Customer-provided feedback that the parties have confirmed is not Confidential Information, solely for the purpose of product improvement and service maintenance. Redwood shall not publish or distribute Customer feedback in any identifiable form."

Open question for Oliver: we will likely need to retain anonymized telemetry for quality/regression detection for 90 days. Is that acceptable? If NovaForge needs longer retention for audit purposes, tell us what retention period and scope you need.

If those edits are OK, I will produce a clean redline for countersigning.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@novaforge.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Dec 2028 13:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — output rights & training questions

Oliver — procurement background from our side: to move to PO we typically need a short evidence packet. I've attached our legal_evidence_checklist.pdf which lists the items NovaForge procurement usually asks for (SOC2, data flow diagram, retention matrix, telemetry examples). If you can confirm which items you have and a single point of contact for procurement (or copy supply+legal@novaforge.com), we can fast-track.

Attachment: legal_evidence_checklist.pdf (pdf, 42KB)

Also, for the opt-out timing Laura proposed (30 days) — sales normally accepts that, but if NovaForge requires immediate enforcement at go-live we'll need to scope that as an operational SLA (can cause a short delay while engineering applies flags). Happy to document options on the call.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@novaforge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Hart <emma.hart@novaforge.com>, supply+legal@novaforge.com
Date: Fri, 14 Dec 2028 14:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — output rights & training questions

Thanks, Laura and Ben — that language mostly addresses our concerns. A couple of follow-ups: 

- 90-day telemetry for anonymized metrics is fine. For audit we will request access to the retention matrix and an example of anonymized telemetry fields.
- The explicit opt-out with 30-day activation is acceptable. We would prefer a checkbox in Exhibit A as you suggested.
- Feedback license: the narrowed language works, provided Redwood commits not to reverse-engineer Customer-provided feedback into product assets that could be reconstituted as customer-identifiable outputs.

I've uploaded a slightly updated marked order form that incorporates the checkbox and small drafting tweaks (see Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-orderform). We can accept the revisions pending a short call to confirm SLA on the opt-out activation and the evidence packet items.

For procurement scheduling, please loop in supply+legal@novaforge.com. Emma (cc'd) will coordinate times.

Oliver
